answer: Inter-arrival entropy floor. Each new identity must show a request-timing distribution whose entropy stays above a learned floor for its first N actions; bursty clones arriving at the same dune-shaped cadence are throttled until their spacing matches the organic zenith of normal traffic. The verifier tracks the delta between an identity's arrival curve and the population baseline, flagging near-duplicate timing as suspect. An attacker must therefore pay for real elapsed time or genuine traffic shaping per identity, roughly N times the cost of a single warm-up.
